sources.entry: TouchBridge - Authenticate with your phone's fingerprint as a free Touch ID keyboard alternative. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/HMAKT99/UnTouchID) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]
UnTouchID - Use your phone's fingerprint to authenticate on any Mac.

summary.one_liner: TouchBridge lets an iPhone's Face ID or Touch ID approve macOS PAM authentication (such as sudo) through a companion app, with a root-run PAM module verifying the phone's signature.
summary.what_it_does: The project provides a privileged PAM module that verifies signed evidence from an iPhone companion app, and a user-level daemon (touchbridged) that transports that evidence between phone and Mac over BLE. Users pair the phone by scanning a QR code, verify fingerprints on the phone, and then enroll administrator-approved keys. The README describes an auto-lock feature that locks the Mac when verified companions leave and cancels the lock on reconnect. It also includes diagnostic modes (--simulator, --interactive, --web) that the README explicitly says cannot approve real PAM. An unpair command clears session state and invalidates the signing capability. v2.0.0 is described as a breaking protocol change requiring the iPhone app to be rebuilt and devices re-paired.
use_cases: approve sudo with iPhone Face ID or Touch ID
use phone biometrics for Mac admin authentication
replace Touch ID prompts on a Mac with a phone
auto-lock Mac when phone leaves range
pair an iPhone with a Mac over Bluetooth
notable: PAM module independently verifies canonical signed evidence against root-managed, per-UID trust
Rejects v1 peers, bare success strings, and unsigned metadata (fail closed)
Installer retires legacy hooks and leaves PAM disabled until explicit enrollment
Auto-lock tracks verified companions and checks actual lock state
Uninstall preserves unrelated PAM entries and backups
caveats: Requires macOS 13+, Xcode with iOS SDK, and a physical iPhone; the iPhone companion app must be built with your own signing team since Homebrew installs only Mac tools
Upgrading from 1.x requires rebuilding the iPhone app, re-pairing, and re-enrolling keys; older release versions must not be used
Android, Apple Watch, browser autofill and Authorization Plugin are not accepted privileged paths; FileVault preboot, Apple Pay and hardware-bound Keychain items are out of scope
